title: Pacemaker fitting
what: The doctor places a small device under the skin below the collarbone. Thin wires run from it through a vein to the heart and help it beat at the right rhythm.
why: When the heart beats too slowly or with pauses, causing fainting, strong weakness, or dizziness from a rhythm problem.
duration: the procedure usually takes 1 to 2 hours; the hospital stay is usually 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor will tell you what to stop and when
Allergies, especially to iodine, antibiotics, or numbing medicines
Which hand you write and work with. The device is usually placed on the other side
If you have had surgery or skin problems near the collarbone

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a heart ultrasound. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for 6 hours before the procedure. Your clinic will give you the exact time.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Take a shower the day before. If you have a lot of chest hair, it may be shaved in hospital.

prepare.title: Things to pack
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes that open at the front, slippers, a phone charger, and the medicines you take every day.

bring: Things for 1 to 3 days in hospital
steps: You change into a gown, an IV is put into a vein, and you are connected to a monitor
You get medicine to relax, sometimes to sleep. It varies
The area under the collarbone is numbed
The doctor makes a small cut and guides the wires through a vein to the heart, using X-ray
The wires are connected to the device and checked
The device is placed under the skin and the cut is stitched
feel: The numbing injection and pressure near the collarbone
Sometimes you can feel the heart rhythm being tested
After the procedure: pain and swelling at the cut for a few days
after: For the first weeks, you usually must not lift the arm on that side above the shoulder or carry heavy things. The doctor will tell you for how long
Keep the wound dry and clean until you are allowed to wash it
You will get a pacemaker card. Carry it with you
Keep your phone at least 15 centimeters from the device. Do not put it in a chest pocket
At the airport, show your card
Always mention your pacemaker before an MRI
The first device check is usually after a few weeks, then regularly
red_flags: Fainting, strong dizziness, shortness of breath, or chest pain: call emergency services
Blood, pus, or swelling or redness at the wound that keeps getting worse
Hiccups that do not stop, or twitching of the chest muscles

faq.q: Can I use a phone with a pacemaker?
faq.a: Yes. Just keep the phone 15 centimeters from the device and hold it to the ear on the other side.

faq.q: Can I have an MRI with a pacemaker?
faq.a: Only if the device is MRI-safe, and only if your cardiologist agrees. Always mention your pacemaker.

faq.q: How long does a pacemaker last?
faq.a: Usually 7 to 12 years. Then the device itself is replaced. The wires are often left in place.

reminders.text: Pacemaker fitting tomorrow. Pack your things, ID, and medicine list. Eat and drink only until the times your clinic gave you.
